sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Everything a person sees or hears is a lesson in divine service, and even apparent chance events are part of Divine Providence, teaching that all details in Torah are instructive.

translations.translation: And 4)
Now, the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov is known,
that everything a person sees or hears is a lesson in the service of G-d.
And the Maggid adds
that everything a person sees and hears, and every occurrence that happens to a person, is for the sake of the service of G-d.
And the explanation of this is,
that even every occurrence is by particular Divine Providence,
and that which is called by the name "chance" is that below, in this world, it is in a manner of chance.
And analogous to what is written,
"If a bird's nest chance to be before you," and our Sages said,
"excluding a prepared one,"
that even though all matters are by particular Divine Providence,
and moreover they are prepared from the prior thought of Adam Kadmon,
nevertheless,
the verse says "if a bird's nest chance to be before you," excluding a prepared one,
for there are matters whose intention is fulfilled when even below they are in a manner of "prepared,"
and there are matters whose intention is fulfilled when below they are in a manner of "chance,"
"if it chance."
And from this it is understood, all the more so, regarding the matters in Torah,
that all its details,
even when they appear externally to be only incidental
(in the manner of chance),
they are instructive.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The attribute of a fortiori (kal vachomer) among the thirteen Torah attributes drawn from the thirteen attributes of mercy in prayer teaches that the drawing down through Torah has a superiority over that through prayer.

translations.translation: And based on this, it can be said,
that this—that the attribute of the thirteen attributes of Torah which is drawn from the thirteen attributes of mercy in prayer is the attribute of kal vachomer—is to teach,
that even though the main drawing down of the thirteen attributes of mercy is in prayer, and through this the drawing down also comes in Torah,
nevertheless,
there is an advantage in the drawing down that is in Torah relative to the drawing down that is in prayer,
in the manner of the attribute of kal vachomer,
for even though the stringent is learned from the lenient,
nevertheless,
it is stringent relative to the lenient.
And as is explained in the maamar,

that this—that we learn the drawing down that is beyond the measure of the elevation through Torah of many from the drawing down through the prayer of many—is a study in the manner of "all the more so,"
kal vachomer.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The difference between Torah and prayer is like the difference between blessing and prayer, where in Torah one becomes a master over the Torah and its flow of influences.

translations.translation: And the matter is,
that the difference between Torah and prayer is analogous to the difference between blessing and prayer.
For in prayer,
the one praying is below and asks that they bestow upon him from above,
and in blessing,
the one who blesses
[he who has the power to bless,
like the kohanim who were given the power to bless]
is above the source from which the blessing is drawn, and commands that the drawing down be to below.
And as the language in the Priestly Blessing, "May the L-rd bless you,"
which is a language of command.
And likewise is it regarding the drawing down of influences through Torah.
For since the crown of Torah is ownerless to all,
behold, it is within the capacity of every single Jew to merit it through engagement in Torah, in a manner that it becomes his Torah
(of the learner),
and he becomes a master, as it were, over the Torah, and all the more so over the drawing down of influences through Torah.
